markdown_report:
Choose **exact feasibility recovery for matched NextItNet interventions**, separating construction success from assignment selection. At 20% progress, repairing diagnostic support remains preferable to changing temporal weighting from one-user replacement results.

Three starting insights guide this choice. First, displayed replacements retain one user in Movies and Electronics; Industrial and CDs show no successful replacement blocks in the supplied summaries. Missing or failed construction is not zero effect. Second, terminal-preserving permutations worsen training-target ranks in Industrial and CDs. Earlier ordering influences these examples without establishing benefits from stronger recency weighting. Third, sampled margins and catalog training-prefix hits concern different competitors; their discrepancy establishes neither sampling failure nor held-out improvement.

Three related-work insights strengthen the repair. Matching certifies all-different feasibility, while additional constraints require sound search [1,6]. Intervention sensitivity depends on assignment probabilities as well as admissibility: minimum-distance optimization changes the measured intervention [7]. Limited overlap and incomplete search require support-specific reporting and explicit unresolved cases [3,8]. Architectural accessibility remains distinct from learned usefulness [2].

| Direction | Existing control | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Construction | Fixed plausibility rules | Greedy failure versus certified infeasibility |
| Mechanism | Reachability and permutations | Learned pathway contributions |
| Interpretation | Paired user summaries | Assignment law, sparse support and incomplete search |

Candidate assessments use originality/potential/difficulty scores; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive / negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Exact feasibility recovery [1,3,6] | 4/6/5 | Useful integration, reusable support audit, small problems; established mathematics, uncertain HR@10 relevance, coupled constraints and selector laws complicate implementation |
| Bidirectional residual patching [4] | 5/7/6 | Useful adaptation, mechanism potential, reusable hooks; established method, corruption dependence, architecture-specific bookkeeping |
| Attribution randomization checks [5] | 2/5/3 | Clear diagnostic addition, detects parameter insensitivity, simple copies; little novelty, no faithfulness guarantee, additional probe cost |

For the selected idea, freeze histories, positions, candidate pools and constraints before scoring. Run greedy construction, validate any incumbent independently, and use capacity-correct matching to prune deterministic constraint search. Preserve feasible incumbents at interruption; distinguish feasibility, distance optimality, certified infeasibility and unresolved search. Validate pruning and optima against independent exhaustive enumeration of tiny instances.

Feasibility recovery and minimum-distance selection answer separate questions. Preserve the original greedy assignment whenever valid; classify rescued assignments under an explicitly specified deterministic selector. Compare selectors on common feasible histories, reporting assignment variability only when assignments are repeatedly drawn under a documented law. Random costs or randomized greedy procedures do not imply uniform feasible sampling [7].

Report rescued users/blocks, deficiencies, joint failures, unresolved fractions and feasibility bounds. Analyze common support and recovered support separately. Retain position-preserving edits, fixed/shared-restricted catalogs, exact ranks, user bootstrap and measured cost. Preserve one NextItNet checkpoint per category and all adapter interfaces; inference remains unchanged. Only pinned four-category validation HR@10 selects model changes. Diagnostic tuning can still overfit selected cases; freeze the protocol before scoring. No improvement is claimed.

References: [1] SciPy matching; [2] effective receptive fields; [3] generalized optimal matching; [4] activation patching; [5] saliency sanity checks; [6] Régin; [7] stochastic interventions; [8] solver statuses. Links appear in `related_work`.

idea.description: Replace greedy-only construction of position-preserving NextItNet diagnostic replacements with a deterministic feasibility audit on the same frozen admissibility pools. Use capacity-correct bipartite matching as a necessary feasibility check and search bound, then explicitly enforce joint sequence and cross-plan constraints. Separate construction recovery from the assignment selector and its sensitivity estimand; fit no additional predictor.
idea.motivation: Displayed dose-one replacement effects in Movies and Electronics each involve only one retained user; the supplied Industrial and CDs summaries expose permutation results without successful replacement blocks. These summaries motivate investigating construction failure, but omitted entries must not be treated as proof of exhaustive failure. Existing definitions explicitly acknowledge that greedy failure does not establish infeasibility. Exact feasibility auditing addresses this measurement limitation before replacement sensitivity motivates training changes. It cannot guarantee additional supported users or better validation HR@10. Minimum-distance selection also changes the intervention mechanism, so its effects cannot automatically be interpreted as a more accurate estimate of the original randomized replacement effect.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected NextItNet, exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint per category, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. No ensembles, other-trial checkpoints, extra datasets, pretrained weights, hidden test access or evaluator changes. This proposal changes diagnostic construction only; retain the existing checkpoint and embedded predictor consistently. No randomized diagnostic copy or alternative assignment method becomes a predictor.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every ModelView interface, including view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Preserve existing full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category. Use only available public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Do not infer compatibility, ownership, unmet needs, review evidence or simulator traits. Unavailable fields and unsupported interpretations remain explicitly unavailable.

Preregister the existing users, cuts, doses, lag bins, replacement repetitions, candidate-generation rules, frequency matching, reachability matching, transition constraints and reuse rules. Retain the existing deterministic prefix selection and sample caps rather than selecting additional cases after seeing effects. Freeze replacement positions, doses, candidate pools, admissibility edges and whole-block predicates before either constructor runs. Do not relax constraints or expand pools in response to solver failure or model scores. Hash and serialize each finite pool, ordered domains, constraints and protocol version. Feasibility conclusions apply to those finite pools, not every catalog item. Where temporal availability cannot be established from available timestamps, report the limitation rather than asserting historical availability. Training transition counts define diagnostic plausibility only; they do not establish behavioral relevance or supply recommendation scores.

For each jointly required recent/older and random/constrained four-plan block, represent intervention positions as slots and admissible replacement IDs as edges. Item capacity and uniqueness must follow the existing protocol: allow cross-plan reuse when permitted, and enforce shared capacity only when explicitly required. Ordinary maximum bipartite matching certifies the corresponding slotwise all-different problem, not arbitrary additional constraints. Use a capacity flow or correctly scoped item copies when appropriate; constraints spanning overlapping reuse groups remain explicit search predicates. Record isolated slots and independently checkable deficiency certificates when available. For unit-capacity graphs, a Hall witness consists of a slot subset whose neighbor set is smaller than that subset. A covering matching does not establish whole-block feasibility.

Use deterministic depth-first branch-and-bound for the small number of replacement slots. Order slots by remaining admissible count, breaking ties by serialized slot ID. Order candidates by a preregistered training-only distance and item ID. Validate capacity, partial predicates and joint constraints as soon as they become decidable, then run an independent complete-assignment checker before accepting any solution. A matching bound on remaining domains can reject branches unable to complete. Do not prune an edge because one maximum matching omitted it. If domain filtering is added, use Régin-style supported-edge filtering or the simpler correctness reference: force the edge and test whether the remaining variables admit a covering matching. Additional joint predicates can invalidate assignments even when every edge passes this necessary test.

Separate two modes. The primary feasibility audit seeks any valid complete block and can stop at the first one; it does not claim minimum distance. An optional selector study minimizes a fixed additive replacement distance among complete valid assignments. Preserve existing protocol distances where possible. If distance uses embeddings, freeze the trained model and identify the selector as model-dependent. Smaller distance need not imply a smaller model response. Initialize optimization with the original greedy assignment only after independent validation; retain that exact assignment for the legacy diagnostic whenever it is valid. With a feasible incumbent of cost U, prune an improvement branch only when a valid lower bound is at least U. A minimum-cost assignment on a relaxation that drops joint predicates supplies a lower bound when its capacity semantics are correct; a simple sum of remaining slot minima is another valid, possibly weaker bound. An arbitrary objective cutoff is not a feasible incumbent. Exhausting an improvement search proves the incumbent optimal, not the original problem infeasible. If lexicographic tie optimality is claimed, continue or constrain search appropriately; otherwise document deterministic first-found handling of equal-cost solutions.

Propose a fixed cap of 10,000 expanded search nodes per block and an aggregate synchronized diagnostic safety cap of 30 seconds per category; these are proposed limits, not measured costs. Define a node as one entered partial-assignment state, including the root, and record matching calls, candidate checks, pool-building work and elapsed time separately. Use single-threaded search, fixed software versions, seed, parameters, domain order and matching implementation. Deterministic node limits improve repeatability but do not equalize computational effort. The wall-time safety cap can change completed work across machines; mark this explicitly. Preserve feasible incumbents at any interruption. Mark unstarted blocks after the aggregate cap as unresolved, never silently exclude them.

Return separate feasibility and optimization fields. Feasibility is certified_feasible after independent checking, certified_infeasible after a sound certificate or exhaustive unpruned feasibility search, or unresolved otherwise. Optimization status is not_requested, feasible_unproven or proven_optimal, with incumbent cost, valid lower bound and gap where available. Time- or node-limited search without an incumbent remains unresolved. A complete feasible incumbent may be scored even when its optimality is unproven. Greedy success with an invalid or missing retained incumbent is an implementation warning, not evidence of infeasibility. Flag conflicting certificates or numerical inconsistencies as errors and exclude affected effects with explicit reasons.

Validate the solver independently before real probes using tiny exhaustive instances and a separate direct constraint checker. Compare feasible sets, optimum values and status classifications. Include surplus candidate values, empty domains, Hall violations without isolated slots, valid covering matchings defeated by pairwise constraints, permitted cross-plan reuse, shared capacities, tied costs, feasible greedy incumbents and interrupted searches before and after finding an incumbent. Check that every pruning rule preserves all truly feasible assignments and that interruption never erases a validated incumbent. Exhaustive tiny tests provide implementation evidence, not a proof for arbitrary code.

Fixed admissibility defines F(h), not a probability distribution over assignments. Explicitly identify the original constructor's law, including seed derivation, candidate order, retries, rejection, failure and repeated-draw rules; do not call it uniform unless established. For randomized selectors, sensitivity is S(q) = E_h E_{a drawn from q(.|h)}[delta(h,a)], conditional on the stated population and completion rules. A deterministic first-feasible or minimum-distance selector defines a different, point-mass intervention. Random edge costs followed by matching do not imply uniform matching samples. Independent RNG repetitions reproduce the implemented law, not an unspecified target law. Do not importance-weight deterministic optimizer outputs to recover an unrestricted random-assignment average. Approximate uniform sampling would require a separate justified algorithm and error characterization and is outside this minimal experiment.

Run greedy and exact construction on identical frozen pools and planned seeds. Report completion separately from sensitivity. Preserve valid legacy assignments rather than replacing them merely because a lower-distance assignment exists. For rescued blocks, report sensitivity under the documented recovery selector as a separate estimand. An optional selector comparison uses common certified-feasible histories, identical positions and counts; report incomplete selector runs rather than conditioning silently on their success. Prespecified distance bands, position-specific distances and candidate characteristics help describe selector differences but do not equate assignment laws or identify causal intent. Repeated assignments per history, if budgeted, characterize assignment variation under each actual law; deterministic selectors have no within-history random-assignment variation.

Separate graph deficiency, exhaustive joint infeasibility, feasible construction, unresolved search and implementation errors. Report eligible users, users with certified-feasible blocks, retained blocks, rescued blocks and support by history length and training frequency. Count each distinct planned block once. If F blocks are certified feasible, I certified infeasible and U unresolved among N = F + I + U error-free planned blocks, eventual feasibility is bounded by [F/N, (F+U)/N]. Report implementation errors separately and provide a conservative bound including them as unknown if a bound over all planned blocks is needed. These are identification bounds conditional on fixed pools, not sampling confidence intervals. For user-level feasibility defined as at least one feasible block, derive bounds from each user's block statuses instead of reusing block fractions. Report cap hits and elapsed times as censored work-to-completion observations; do not substitute a cutoff for a completed runtime or average only completed runs as an unrestricted runtime estimate.

Report effects separately on common successful support and exact-only support; their union changes the supported population. On common support, distinguish changing the assignment selector from changing the constructor. Do not attribute changed averages solely to better estimation or apply unsupported selection weights. Multiple planned corruption draws do not add users. Retain full raw assignments, IDs, positions, distances, seeds, solver statuses, failures and counts so support-specific summaries can be recomputed.

Keep in-place edits, unchanged terminal item, occupied positions, left padding and timestamps. Gather the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1; exclude empty histories. Inputs contain training-prefix interactions only, without the target occurrence or subsequent sequence context. Preserve fixed original-full-prefix eligibility, target retained once, PAD exclusion, repeated-target flags, shared restricted catalogs, inserted-item decomposition, exact chunked ranks with ascending-ID ties, and existing identity/causality/padding controls. Structural reachability remains an accessibility control, not evidence of useful learned influence. Encode each unique history once, stream catalog scores and validate rank counting against exhaustive synthetic sorting.

Average prescribed assignment repetitions within prefixes and prefixes within users. Resample whole users within categories, retaining every selected user's prefixes, perturbations, solver statuses and paired method results; recompute support-specific statistics in each replicate. Keep assignment Monte Carlo summaries separate from between-user uncertainty. Intervals remain exploratory and fragile with few clusters; return them unavailable below two supported users, and flag bootstrap replicates with undefined support. Compute an equal-weight four-category macro only when all four categories have defined measurements; do not pool users across categories or replace missing categories. Preserve RNG states and individual module modes in finally, using a diagnostic RNG independent of training.

Return measured metrics, metric_definitions, protocol, raw assignment records, support denominators, unavailable reasons, solver bounds and synchronized cost. The interpretation prompt must distinguish construction feasibility, selection mechanism, conditional sensitivity, identification bounds and sampling uncertainty. All computation counts against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; the host remains authoritative for accounting. Freeze constraints, distances and selectors before observing their score effects to reduce diagnostic overfitting. Repeatedly selecting protocols from training-prefix sensitivity can favor memorized transitions, popularity-matched candidates or unusually easy supported users. Monitor these strata without asserting causal preferences. The unchanged host macro validation HR@10 alone selects any subsequent model change; diagnostic support recovery is not a validation improvement.
idea.pseudocode:
Record unchanged protocol, planned blocks, finite-pool hashes, constraints,
reuse semantics, selector laws, software versions and solver caps.
Validate matching, propagation, bounds and statuses against an independent
exhaustive tiny-instance checker, including interrupted searches.
Save RNG states and individual module modes.
try:
    Set the category's single trained NextItNet to evaluation mode.
    For each existing deterministic training-prefix intervention block:
        pools = freeze_existing_candidate_pools(block)
        greedy = run_existing_greedy(pools, unchanged_constraints)
        incumbent = greedy only if independent_complete_checker(greedy)
        graph = build_capacity_correct_slot_item_graph(pools, reuse_rules)
        bound, certificate = maximum_matching_or_capacity_flow(graph)
        if a checked certificate proves required slots cannot be filled:
            feasibility = certified_infeasible
        else:
            Search assignments deterministically within node/safety caps:
                Select remaining slot by domain size, then stable slot ID.
                Try candidates in predefined distance/item-ID order.
                Reject violated capacities and decidable joint predicates.
                Prune if remaining matching cannot cover remaining slots.
                Never prune an edge just because one matching omitted it.
                If optimizing and a validated incumbent exists:
                    Prune only if valid cost lower bound >= incumbent cost.
                Independently check every complete assignment.
                Preserve each better validated incumbent.
                In feasibility-only mode, stop after first valid completion.
            Classify feasibility separately from distance optimality.
            Exhausted improvement search with incumbent => proven_optimal.
            Interrupted search without incumbent => unresolved.
        Preserve original valid greedy assignment for legacy effects.
        Log pools, assignments, certificates, statuses, bounds, nodes and cost.
        Score complete independently checked plans only:
            Preserve positions, padding, terminal item and eligibility.
            Encode unique histories; gather maximum nonpadding index.
            Stream exact ranks on fixed and shared restricted catalogs.
        If aggregate safety cap fires:
            Mark remaining planned blocks unresolved and stop.
    Report construction outcomes, errors, rescued users/blocks and F/I/U counts.
    Compute feasibility identification bounds separately from sampling intervals.
    Summarize common-support and recovered-support effects separately.
    Label each sensitivity summary with its actual assignment selector/law.
    If comparing selectors, use common feasible histories and report censoring.
    Average draws within prefix, then prefixes within user.
    Bootstrap whole users within category, preserving paired records/statuses.
finally:
    Restore RNG states and every saved module mode.
Return metrics, metric_definitions, protocol, raw records and measured cost.
Aggregate equal-category summaries only when all four results are defined.
Keep the unchanged pinned host validation HR@10 authoritative.

originality.positive: Combines exact assignment recovery, independently validated feasibility, explicit assignment mechanisms and support-specific effect reporting in the existing NextItNet intervention adapter.
originality.negative: Matching, constraint search, stochastic-intervention estimands and complete-case reporting are established; the contribution remains a targeted diagnostic integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish construction failures from restrictive pools and identify selector-induced changes, making later single-model experiments more defensible.
future_potential.negative: Exact search may recover little support, deterministic recovery changes the intervention estimand, and no relationship with validation HR@10 improvement has been established.

code_difficulty.positive: Doses one and two create small assignment problems, existing pools and scoring hooks are reusable, and inference requires no modification.
code_difficulty.negative: Capacity semantics, coupled constraints, sound pruning, independent solver tests, interrupted-search statuses and assignment-aware aggregation add substantial implementation work.

related_work.title: SciPy: maximum_bipartite_matching
contributions: Provides maximum-cardinality matching for sparse bipartite graphs.
Supports distinguishing greedy assignment failure from slotwise infeasibility under appropriate uniqueness constraints.
limitations: Does not enforce arbitrary whole-sequence or cross-plan constraints.
Feasibility is conditional on the supplied graph and correct capacity semantics.

related_work.title: Understanding the Effective Receptive Field in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
contributions: Distinguishes effective influence from theoretical receptive-field extent.
Motivates separating NextItNet architectural accessibility controls from measured intervention sensitivity.
limitations: Does not establish useful temporal dependence in this recommendation benchmark.
Gradient influence alone does not identify causal user preferences.

related_work.title: Generalized Optimal Matching Methods for Causal Inference
contributions: Provides a framework for matching and weighting with attention to balance and overlap.
Motivates explicit reporting of the population supported by successful diagnostic matches.
limitations: Matching model-input interventions does not supply behavioral causal identification.
Broader-population conclusions require assumptions beyond successful assignments.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Studies how corruption design and output metrics affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates a later diagnostic comparing restoration and destruction of NextItNet residual-branch activations.
limitations: The proposed NextItNet adaptation is unvalidated.
Patching conclusions remain conditional on corruption, intervention site and metric.

related_work.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
contributions: Introduces parameter-randomization checks for attribution dependence on learned weights.
Offers a control for future NextItNet influence maps.
limitations: Passing randomization checks does not establish attribution faithfulness.
Diagnostic randomized copies must remain outside training and prediction.

related_work.title: A Filtering Algorithm for Constraints of Difference in CSPs
contributions: Connects all-different constraint feasibility and supported-edge filtering to bipartite matching.
Motivates retaining an assignment edge only when it belongs to some variable-covering matching.
limitations: All-different consistency does not establish feasibility under additional joint predicates.
Independent complete-assignment validation remains necessary for the proposed adapter.

related_work.title: Causal Inference With Stochastic Interventions
contributions: Formalizes interventions through their assignment distributions.
Motivates distinguishing sensitivity under a randomized replacement law from sensitivity under a deterministic optimizer.
limitations: The proposed model-input sensitivity analysis does not inherit behavioral causal identification.
Fixed admissibility alone supplies neither assignment probabilities nor the assumptions needed for causal conclusions.

related_work.title: OR-Tools CP-SAT troubleshooting and solver status guidance
contributions: Distinguishes feasible solutions, proven infeasibility, optimality and incomplete search.
Motivates preserving feasible incumbents and explicitly reporting unresolved capped searches.
limitations: Status guidance does not verify a custom solver's correctness.
OR-Tools is not required or assumed installed; the proposed implementation uses available Python and SciPy capabilities.

related_work.title: SCIP primal solution and objective-bound documentation
contributions: Distinguishes feasible-solution-backed primal bounds from objective cutoffs.
Supports correct incumbent initialization and interpretation of exhausted improvement searches.
limitations: Documentation does not establish validity of custom lower bounds or joint constraints.
SCIP is a methodological reference, not an additional required dependency.

related_work.title: Testing Global Constraints
contributions: Motivates independently checking constraint implementations and propagator correctness.
Supports exhaustive tiny-instance comparisons of feasible sets, pruning and optimum values.
limitations: Finite tests do not prove correctness on every production instance.
A checker sharing the same faulty predicates or pruning implementation would provide weak independence.

related_work.title: A Polynomial-Time Approximation Algorithm for the Permanent of a Matrix With Nonnegative Entries
contributions: Provides foundational methods related to approximately uniform sampling of perfect matchings.
Illustrates why uniform feasible sampling requires a justified algorithm rather than random costs followed by optimization.
limitations: Does not directly provide a uniform sampler for the adapter's arbitrary joint constraints.
Its machinery is unnecessary for the proposed minimal feasibility audit.

related_work.title: Restricted assignment mechanisms and design-aware analysis
contributions: Motivates aligning analysis with the actual restricted assignment mechanism.
Supports documenting retries, rejection, selection and common support when comparing replacement procedures.
limitations: The recommendation perturbation protocol is an adaptation rather than a validated application.
Design-aware analysis cannot convert unsupported model perturbations into real-world preference effects.

related_work.title: Gurobi parameter documentation: deterministic work limits
contributions: Explains deterministic work limits under controlled hardware and solver settings.
Motivates fixed search-work caps and separate elapsed-cost reporting.
limitations: A custom Python node budget does not inherit Gurobi's reproducibility guarantees.
Equal node counts need not imply equal computational effort; Gurobi is not a required dependency.

related_work.title: IBM documentation: optimizer determinism and optimization limits
contributions: Discusses determinism, parallel execution and optimization limits.
Motivates fixing thread mode, ordering, versions and parameters when reporting capped search.
limitations: Parallel synchronization can complicate strict stopping-point guarantees.
The proposal uses single-threaded diagnostic search and does not require IBM optimization software.

related_work.title: Censored-runtime research
contributions: Addresses runtime observations censored by execution cutoffs.
Motivates distinguishing observed work before interruption from completed time-to-solution.
limitations: Dropping interrupted cases or substituting cutoff times does not recover unrestricted runtime averages.
More elaborate runtime inference requires assumptions beyond the proposed descriptive audit.

related_work.title: Cluster-bootstrap study
contributions: Motivates resampling whole clusters to preserve within-subject dependence.
Supports user-level resampling that retains prefixes, perturbations and paired selector results within each category.
limitations: Few supported users make bootstrap intervals fragile.
Additional perturbations do not increase the number of independent users or correct protocol-selection bias.
